About

I'm Robert Calef, a 4th year PhD student at MIT CSAIL.

My scientific work has been an eclectic mix of developing computational methods to extract insight from large biological datasets. During my PhD, I've worked on multimodal protein modeling and representation learning, and lately have been focused on developing sequence-level models of gene regulation. I'm fortunate to have two great scientific advisors, Manolis Kellis and Marinka Zitnik, and to be supported by a NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.

In my past lives, I earned my BS in bioinformatics at UC Santa Cruz (go banana slugs!), worked on ancient DNA in UCSC's Paleogenomics Lab, helped create hundreds of high-quality genome assemblies at Dovetail Genomics, and was a core contributor to the world's first blood-based multicancer early detection test (which may be FDA approved very soon!) at GRAIL. Along the way, I was extremely lucky to get to work with and learn from amazing people.

Outside of work, I am a prolific consumer of many forms of media, including films, novels, video games, and excessively complicated cooking recipes. In an attempt to mitigate my horrible long-term memory, I've begun logging the films and novels I've enjoyed recently. If you'd like to chat, please reach out at rcalef[at]mit.edu
